profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at an economic advisory firm preparing a central-bank client workshop on a new contagion-intervention toolkit based on research about default contagion under partial information. The quant workstream has finished the asymptotic policy analysis and simulation runs, while the client delivery workstream is assembling the workshop deck, appendix, and post-meeting model materials. The agenda is to align on which prior deck is being updated, what results are considered final enough to circulate, what belongs in the technical appendix, and how the model outputs will be handed off for the client package. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the Wednesday steering-committee deliverables, responsibilities, and timing between the research and delivery teams.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: Financial network modeling, stress testing, contagion simulations, asymptotic policy analysis
members.background: Lena leads the firm's systemic-risk analytics team and previously worked in a central-bank research unit; she is comfortable translating academic models into advisory tools but still thinks primarily in terms of model integrity and methodological traceability.
members.private_state: She wants the workshop materials to preserve the nuance of the research, especially the partial-information setting and the monotonic intervention logic, and she is worried that an overly simplified deck will cause the client to overgeneralize the results or misuse intermediate simulation outputs.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the March deck,' they mean the March 18 methodology deck that incorporated partner comments and the latest framing of the partial-information model.
If the 'numbers are locked,' that means the qualitative pattern and ranking of scenarios are stable enough that only minor numerical drift might still occur after a cleanup rerun.

An 'appendix on the intervention policy' should include the monotonicity intuition, the keep-intervening continuation rule, and enough technical caveats for economists to understand where the asymptotic results do and do not apply.

A 'model package handoff' naturally means notebooks, parameter files, and a short README delivered to the internal analytics repository, after which the delivery team will format any client-facing tables.

members.name: Aaron Mills
members.expertise: Executive communications, regulatory client coordination, deck production, cross-workstream delivery management
members.background: Aaron manages high-stakes deliverables for financial-regulation clients and previously worked in a strategy PMO at a bank; he is strong on timelines, version control, and making technical work consumable by policy and executive audiences.
members.private_state: He wants a clean, stable package that design and compliance can finalize without reopening content late in the process, and he is concerned about last-minute changes breaking exhibit numbering, messaging consistency, or client expectations around what materials they will receive after the workshop.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the March deck,' they mean the March 12 steering-committee deck that the client already saw and that all Wednesday materials should visibly build from.
If the 'numbers are locked,' that means the exact values, labels, and chart ordering are final enough to pass into design and compliance with no further reruns.
An 'appendix on the intervention policy' is a narrow backup section supporting the three main charts in the client deck, not a self-contained technical note.
A 'model package handoff' means an exhibit-ready Excel workbook and labeled tables in the client delivery folder so the package can be reused immediately in deck production and follow-up materials.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'March deck' is the base document
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss updating 'the March deck' for Wednesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the March 18 internal methodology deck revised after partner comments, with fuller framing of partial information and the intervention logic.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the March 12 client-facing steering-committee deck already circulated externally and used as the visible baseline for Wednesday's workshop.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There really were multiple March decks, both are recent, and each participant has one salient March artifact in mind; because both only need a baseline in the conversation, the phrase feels specific enough and never triggers clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the simulation results should be 'locked' before they go into the materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'locked' means the directional findings are stable and any remaining rerun would only slightly adjust figures without changing the story.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'locked' means exact scenario values, labels, and chart contents are frozen and safe to hand to design and compliance without further change.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'locked' is a routine progress term that usually signals readiness, so both hear confirmation of maturity rather than a need to define the threshold precisely.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to include 'an appendix on the intervention policy.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the appendix includes the monotonicity result, the rule that once intervention starts it should continue on that bank, the partial-information caveat, and brief proof-style intuition for the asymptotic claims.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the appendix is limited to backup exhibits and a concise note explaining the three headline policy charts, with technical depth reserved for a later paper or separate note.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Appendix work is often treated as supporting material rather than a primary decision item, so the phrase sounds aligned even though each person imagines a different boundary around what the appendix contains.

misalignment_points.topic: How the model package will be handed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about 'handing off the model package' after the workshop.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to deliver notebooks, configuration files, and a README to the internal analytics repository, expecting the delivery team to transform outputs into client-ready formats as needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects a client-ready Excel pack with named tabs matching deck exhibits in the delivery folder so it can be reused directly in follow-up materials and meeting notes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are discussing the same downstream need and use a familiar handoff phrase, but each relies on the default workflow of their own function and assumes the other sees that workflow as standard.

turns.inner_thought: Before we get too far into production, I need to anchor Wednesday on the March 18 methodology deck, not the older client version, because that is where the partial-information framing and the cleaner intervention logic landed after partner comments. If we strip too much out of the backup, the client will walk away with the policy pattern but none of the conditions under which it holds. I need the main story and the appendix on the intervention policy to line up so nobody treats the simulation outputs as universal prescriptions.
turns.utterance: I just want to make sure Wednesday's workshop materials build cleanly from the March deck and that the intervention story reads the same way in the main deck and in backup.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we are obviously talking about the March 12 steering deck the client already saw. Design has already set that structure up, so as long as quant is layering updates onto that baseline, we avoid churn and keep continuity with what the client expects. I mainly need to know what gets swapped in and what remains untouched.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's how I'm approaching it as well. Design is already aligned around the March deck, so what I mainly need from your side is which pieces quant wants to add or swap for the updated version.

turns.inner_thought: The latest runs are mature enough that the qualitative pattern is stable. The heterogeneous network cases now make the monotonic intervention logic visible, and the continuation rule is much clearer than it was in the earlier calibration. I still might clean up a baseline seed or formatting issue, but nothing that should change scenario ranking or the interpretation. So in my mind the numbers are locked for deck purposes.
turns.utterance: The new simulation set is basically locked at this point, and it now shows the intervention pattern and the continued-support rule much more clearly across the heterogeneous network cases.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. I need exact chart content frozen once I send it on; otherwise we risk reopening the whole chain.
turns.utterance: That's great. Once the numbers are locked, I can send the charts through design and compliance without reopening exhibit numbering.

turns.inner_thought: I need the appendix on the intervention policy to do real work, not just sit there as a thin backup. It should give the intuition for why intervention should continue once initiated on a given bank, and it has to say enough about the partial-information setting that an economist in the room understands the interpretation boundary. Not a full paper, but more than a captioned chart pack.
turns.utterance: I would also like to include an appendix on the intervention policy that gives a short explanation of why intervention should continue once begun and how the partial-information assumption changes the interpretation.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds fine as long as it stays in the appendix and supports the three headline policy slides. I do not want the client deck turning into a technical note. A concise backup section with enough context for questions is exactly what we need; anything deeper can be handled later if they ask for it.
turns.utterance: Agreed. An appendix on the intervention policy will be useful as backup for the three main policy slides, and it should help us answer questions without making the client deck feel too technical.

turns.inner_thought: After the workshop I can hand off the model package by pushing the notebooks, parameter files, and a short README into the analytics repository. I just need to tidy the parameter file and attach the latest run notes so the team has traceability on the calibration. From there delivery can format whatever they need for the client-facing side.
turns.utterance: On the follow-up, I can hand off the model package right after the workshop once I tidy the parameter file and push the run notes from the latest calibration.

turns.inner_thought: Excellent. We will need that model package quickly because the follow-up note will likely reuse the workshop exhibits, and I want the team to be able to drop the same tables straight into the client delivery folder with the same exhibit labels. If that package lands promptly in a usable format, we avoid a second production cycle.
turns.utterance: Perfect. The follow-up note will need the model package quickly so the team can drop the same tables into the client folder and reuse the exhibit labels.

turns.inner_thought: I should flag the cleanup rerun, but only lightly so nobody overreacts. It is just a baseline cleanup pass, and I do not expect any story-level movement. In my terms the numbers are still locked because the pattern is stable; if a figure shifts a bit, that should not matter for the deck narrative.
turns.utterance: One small caveat from my side: I may do a cleanup rerun tonight on the baseline cases, but I don't expect any story-level change before the deck update goes out.

Since she said no story-level change, I assume the charts are effectively frozen and any cleanup will not affect values or ordering in what goes to design.
